stem.en: Which two of these mixtures show the Tyndall effect? (i) air and dust particles (ii) copper sulfate and water (iii) starch and water (iv) acetone and water

explanation.en: Dust in air is made of particles that scatter light, like the sunbeam in a dark room. Starch in water is a colloid, so it scatters light too. Copper sulfate dissolves to give a clear blue solution, and acetone mixes with water to give a solution, so neither shows a path. A coloured liquid is not the same as a cloudy one: copper sulfate is blue, but its beam stays hidden.

hints.en: Which of these four are solutions?
A solution never shows the Tyndall effect.
